GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1298 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time.
  • To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs).
  • The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time. Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans?

To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space.

The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons.

The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games.

With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars.

Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics.

Recent findings suggest that starfield even has a "fresh game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it.

The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining.

Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky.

According to recent reports, it's grown so much over the years that its original space exploration premise has been buried by content like fully customizable space stations, actual cities and towns with alien NPCs, gigantic kaiju-like beasts, and... fishing. The endless free updates have pushed the roleplaying aspects deeper, as Hello Games are really making it the "forever" space game.

In a recent development, most importantly though, you can be the greatest bad guy the virtually infinite universe has ever seen, controlling entire pirate fleets and firing on (or stealing) every spaceship that you come across. It might be a bit aimless for some, but if you love a "forever game" then NMS can be the biggest space-set criminal sim ever created.

Though it took too long, Star Wars has gotten really close to cracking the GTA formula in outer space in a shameless enough way. 2024's Star Wars Outlaws is, to this date, the closest thing we've received to a space-set sandbox directly inspired by Rockstar's huge hits.

By letting us fully embrace the Han Solo-like scoundrel fantasy, Massive Entertainment delivered a Star Wars adventure that's all about breaking the law. Hell, they even got a wanted system in there that has protagonist Kay Vess dodging stormtroopers and rival criminal factions like you would in Vice City.

It has been revealed that star Wars Outlaws' take on GTA isn't just about the surface-level gameplay and open structure; it also understands much of its playful tone, moral ambiguity, and stressful rhythm. Jumping between several medium-sized maps set on different planets and spaceship sections breaks up the experience a little, so it never quite reaches that level of seamless immersion, but if anyone wants to do a focused version of GTA in space in the future, Massive's attempt is the one game that got at least halfway there.

Before we go (and before you go back to playing GTA VI), we should remember the daring video games that, for a variety of reasons, never got to realize their visions of a crime-oriented space adventure.

Remember Star Wars 1313 and Visceral Games' cancelled project? It's hard not to spot some of their DNA surviving in Outlaws. As Luke Skywalker wisely stated before noping out, "No one's ever really gone." Lucasfilm loves that, and it extends to binned video games too, thankfully. Even the elusive Battlefront 3 is back from the dead now.

In a recent development, bethesda also had something going at some point with "Prey 2", a bounty hunter action game set in a cyberpunk-ish alien world. Before it was canned, it dropped one of the coolest CG game trailers ever made and teased us with a Blade Runner-esque future long before Cyberpunk hit our consoles.

It has been revealed that looking at the future, Ubisoft's Beyond Good & Evil 2 wants to go substantial and lawless, potentially iterating on Star Wars Outlaws and other open-world crime sims. But years after its announcement and many mind-boggling development news updates, it's hard to believe it's really ever coming out. Maybe the "Before GTA VI" meme can morph into "Before BG&E2" now that Rockstar's masterpiece is finally out.

Sources indicate that ultimately, Rockstar is Rockstar. A one-of-a-kind megastudio with nearly unlimited resources. Trying to replicate GTA does — either on Earth or among the stars — would be an Icarus flight in the making for most studios. There are some GTA-flavored space adventures out there, as we've shown, but we're still waiting for the one. Something that matches the deep storytelling, complete freedom, and cheeky tone of Rockstar's iconic series. OK, I gotta get out of here, I'm too hip for this, I gotta play GTA VI some more.

It has been revealed that jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive.

  • Cardi B, Travis Scott, Dua Lipa, Justice, Lana Del Rey — these are just some of the artists whose music can be heard on dozens of in-game radio stations.
  • GTA 6's plethora of licensed music has led to some viral moments, like the clip of streamer caseoh rocking out to Ariana Grande in real life while chilling out in a car in the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI has quite a stacked soundtrack.

Cardi B, Travis Scott, Dua Lipa, Justice, Lana Del Rey — these are just some of the artists whose music can be heard on dozens of in-game radio stations.

GTA 6's plethora of licensed music has led to some viral moments, like the clip of streamer caseoh rocking out to Ariana Grande in real life while chilling out in a car in the game.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Thankfully, Rockstar Games has kept streamers and content creators in mind and gave them an easy way to shut off licensed music. Here's how to do it.

Simply pause the game by pressing the option or menu button on your controller.

Next, scroll down to the Settings option.

In the Settings menu, head to the very last tab labeled Audio.

Finally, scroll down to Mute Licensed Music and toggle this option on.

This option will mute all the licensed music in the game and ensure your streams and videos don't get taken down.

It has been revealed that there are some things to note. Rockstar Games does not provide any royalty-free replacement music. If a licensed song is playing on the radio in-game, owners won't hear anything until a radio show host or original song comes on. With that said, original music created for the game will continue to play. In addition, captions for licensed music will still appear on screen even though the music won't be audible.

You can always roll the dice and hope a song played on the radio in GTA 6 doesn't take down your stream or clip. But, this Mute Licensed Music option will help you avoid any potential issues.

Topics Gaming Video Games Grand Theft Auto.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The ECHR published its decision on Tuesday, saying that Turkey must release Atalay and allow him to take up his seat in the Turkish parliament.
  • The court ruled that his continued detention had been intended to silence him and undermine political pluralism.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) ruled against Turkey over the detention of human rights lawyer and elected lawmaker Can Atalay.

The ECHR published its decision on Tuesday, saying that Turkey must release Atalay and allow him to take up his seat in the Turkish parliament.

The court ruled that his continued detention had been intended to silence him and undermine political pluralism.

It ordered Turkey to pay him €32,500 (about $35,700) in compensation.

The judges stressed that Atalay's case should not be considered separately, but rather in the wider context of the detention of political opponents, human rights activists and journalists in Turkey.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that turkey was among the original signatories of the European Convention on Human Rights. Yet it has previously refused to comply with the court's decisions in the cases of rights activist Osman Kavala and prominent Kurdish politician Selahattin Demirtas.

As a lawyer, Atalay represented victims in numerous social and political cases in Turkey, as well as in freedom of speech cases involving journalists and writers.

He was also among the leading voices in the 2013 Gezi protests, which the government called an attempted coup.

Because of his involvement in the protests, Atalay, along with seven others, was sentenced to 18 years in prison in April 2022 for "aiding and abetting an attempted coup.".

Continuing his struggle from the infamous Silivri prison, Atalay ran as a candidate for the Workers' Party of Turkey (TIP) in the 2023 parliamentary elections.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A candidate for the earthquake-hit province of Hatay, he won his seat but was denied release despite multiple rulings by the Constitutional Court, Turkey's top court.

According to recent reports, his parliamentary status was revoked in 2024, a decision the Constitutional Court later overturned. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's party stopped the opposition from formally reading the decision in parliament.

Although a year later an opposition lawmaker read the decision in parliament, Atalay remains in jail.

After the ECHR's ruling was published, TIP leader Erkan Bas took to social media to call for Atalay's release and the restoration of his parliamentary mandate.

#70633. Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1265 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1265 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that an eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function.
  • The findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less important than how they use that time.
  • The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that an eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function. Researchers found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the widespread assumption that screen time is necessarily harmful to developing brains.

The findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less important than how they use that time. Activities that encourage learning, creativity, and problem-solving could be particularly valuable. Researchers emphasize that the goal should not be to eliminate screen time, but to balance it with physical activity and mentally stimulating experiences.

The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers. A sedentary lifestyle has been linked to poorer academic performance, while regular exercise is known to support brain function, particularly in adults. However, scientists still have much to learn about how physical activity, sitting, and screen use during childhood influence thinking abilities later in adolescence.

These questions are especially key because childhood and adolescence are critical periods of brain development. Changes in attention, memory, and learning during these years can have lasting consequences, potentially influencing educational opportunities and career paths well into adulthood.

To investigate these relationships, Finnish researchers examined how screen time, physical activity, and sedentary behavior from childhood through adolescence were associated with cognitive performance in teenagers. They also explored whether the connections differed between boys and girls and whether the intensity of physical activity made a difference.

More Screen Time Linked to Better Thinking Skills.

One of the study's most unexpected findings was that greater screen time throughout childhood was associated with better cognitive processing in adolescence.

Cognitive processing refers to the mental abilities people use to take in information, pay attention, remember details, learn new things, and solve problems. These abilities play an important role in school performance and everyday decision-making.

The findings challenge the idea that all screen time should be viewed as harmful. However, the researchers caution that the relationship may depend on what children are actually doing while using digital devices. Watching videos, playing games that require strategic thinking, and engaging in educational activities may involve very different levels of mental effort.

Sources indicate that "The findings suggest that screen time can support children's and adolescents' cognitive processing. Presumably, the essential point here is what kind of things they do in their screen time. Teachers and parents should encourage children to use devices and screens in such ways that promote active thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and learning," states Doctoral Researcher Petri Jalanko from the University of Jyväskylä.

"We should not regard screen time solely as harmful but seek balance between physical activity and screen time that promotes active thinking," Jalanko summarizes.

Exercise Affects Boys' and Girls' Brains Differently.

The researchers also uncovered a more complicated picture of how physical activity relates to thinking and memory.

In a recent development, among girls, spending more time engaged in light-intensity physical activity since childhood was associated with better working memory during adolescence. For boys, greater participation in guided physical activity over the same period was linked to stronger working memory.

Working memory is the brain's ability to temporarily hold and use information. It allows someone to remember instructions while completing a task, keep track of numbers during mental calculations, or follow a conversation while processing new information.

Sources indicate that light-intensity physical activity generally includes relatively gentle movements that do not substantially increase breathing or heart rate. Guided physical activity refers to exercise carried out with some form of instruction or supervision, such as organized sports or structured exercise sessions.

Sources indicate that the differences between boys and girls suggest that the relationship between exercise and brain health may depend on more than simply how much a person moves. The type of activity, how it is organized, and the individual's sex could all play a role.

Another Surprising Finding About Physical Activity.

Sources indicate that the study produced another counterintuitive result. Teenagers who reported spending less time in unsupervised physical activity tended to perform better on measures of cognitive processing.

Yet when researchers used wearable sensors to objectively measure movement and heart rate, they found no association between overall physical activity or sedentary time and cognitive performance.

Sources indicate that one possible explanation is that wearable devices measure movement without revealing what a person is actually doing. For example, a sensor may record periods of sitting or physical activity, but it cannot determine whether someone is solving a difficult problem, studying, participating in an organized activity, or simply resting.

This distinction could help explain why questionnaire responses revealed relationships that were not apparent in the sensor measurements.

Industry observers note that "Our study indicates that the connections of physical activity and sedentary behavior to cognitive processing are complex and depend on the sex, the type and assessment method of physical activity and sedentary time. Moreover, boys and girls may benefit from different types of physical activity in view of brain health," Jalanko adds.

Sources indicate that "However, we need more intervention studies to find out causal relations and sex differences in this respect. Moreover, it is important to examine more specifically the effects of the intensity of physical activity on changes taking place in cognitive processing.".

What the Eight-Year Study Revealed.

The findings come from an eight-year follow-up conducted as part of the PANIC study, a long-running Finnish research project investigating children's physical activity and nutrition.

In a recent development, the current analysis included 260 participants, consisting of 124 girls and 136 boys. Their average age at the adolescent assessment was 15.8 years.

Researchers collected information about physical activity and sedentary behavior using both questionnaires and wearable devices that combined heart rate monitoring with movement measurements. This approach allowed them to compare participants' reported activities with data collected by sensors.

In a recent development, to evaluate cognitive abilities, the researchers used the CogState test battery, a collection of computerized assessments designed to measure aspects of mental performance. The tests examined learning, attention, and working memory.

In a recent development, importantly, the findings show associations rather than cause and effect. They do not establish that increasing screen time will improve a child's thinking abilities or that reducing certain types of exercise will produce cognitive benefits. Intervention studies, in which researchers deliberately change participants' activities and measure the results, are needed to determine whether these relationships are causal.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, the results offer an crucial perspective on the continuing debate over children's screen use. Rather than treating all time spent with digital devices as equally harmful, the researchers suggest paying closer attention to whether those activities encourage active thinking and learning.

The research also highlights the importance of considering different forms of physical activity rather than focusing exclusively on the total amount of exercise children receive.

Together, the findings suggest that supporting healthy brain development may require a more nuanced approach, one that combines physical activity with opportunities for learning, creativity, and mental engagement, including those that take place on screens.

The study was published in the scientific journal Pediatric Exercise Science.

The band delivered an emotional set packed with hits and gave a special shoutout to Mexico and its president. The British collective also brought out veteran guitarist Johnny Marr and Argentine rapper Trueno as special guests.

“I f— with Mexico because you have a revolutionary spirit here,” Gorillaz frontman Damon Albarn told the crowd. “This is an inspirational country.”.

Sources indicate that the first day of the festival’s 16th edition featured established acts and rising artists across indie, soul, electro-pop, folk and contemporary rap. Female artists — performing solo or with their bands — were especially well represented, including CHVRCHES, Violet Grohl, Olivia Dean, CMAT, Grace Ives, Anna Luna and Darianna Everett.

Some 72,000 people attended the rock-filled day, according to promoter Ocesa. They also caught sets from James Blake, Mumford & Sons, Yung Lean, The Kooks, Jamie xx and Durand Jones & The Indications, among others.

In a recent development, the enthusiastic crowd kept the energy high throughout the marathon day of music, which stretched into the early hours of Saturday (Nov. 21) at Curva 4, the Formula 1 venue in Mexico City.

Saturday’s lineup included Twenty One Pilots, The Offspring, Balu Brigada, Pierce the Veil, Underworld, Sébastien Tellier and Peaches and more. On Sunday (Nov. 21), The Strokes will be headlining the festival. Other performing acts will include The xx, Lola Young, Lil Yachty, The Black Crowes, Santigold, Manic Street Preachers, Tricky and more.

Here are five of the best moments from day one of Corona Capital 2026.

In a recent development, gorillaz, Damon Albarn and Jamie Hewlett’s famous collective, returned to Mexico City after eight years for a memorable performance, with guitarist Johnny Marr and Argentine rapper Trueno joining as special guests. Albarn, the former Blur frontman, also praised Mexico’s “revolutionary spirit” and gave a shout-out to President Claudia Sheinbaum.

Gorillaz headlined the festival’s opening day with a set focused mainly on their 2026 album The Mountain and the hits that have made the group one of pop’s biggest acts.

Industry observers note that marr, former guitarist for The Smiths, joined the band for “The Empty Dream Machine” and “Casablanca.” Trueno came out for “THE MANIFESTO” and freestyled on “Clint Eastwood,” which closed the set. Mexican singer Luisa Almaguer also joined Gorillaz for “Latin Simone (Que Pasa Contigo),” originally recorded with the late Cuban star Ibrahim Ferrer for the band’s self-titled debut album.

The Scottish trio, led by vocalist Lauren Mayberry, surprised Mexican fans with new songs set to appear on their upcoming album, All The King’s Men. New singles “Roses” and “Evil,” which will be featured on the LP due in January, stood out for their memorable melodies and expansive synths. Classics like “Forever” and “Miracle” made for emotional moments with longtime fans.

Backed by her rock band, the singer-songwriter showed she’s carrying on the family name with a direct, high-energy set featuring songs like “Bug In The Cake,” “THUM,” “Last Day I Loved You” and “Cool Buzz.”.

In a recent development, swedish rapper Yung Lean, who won over the internet and a generation of listeners with his cloud rap and contemporary hip-hop sound, was also one of the day’s most anticipated acts. He took the main stage to show why he’s considered one of today’s standout artists in the genre, performing songs including “Ghostown,” “Kyoto,” “Forever Yung,” “Pikachu,” “Yoshi City” and “STORM II,” as well as his remix of Charli xcx’s “360.”.

Sources indicate that the U.S. band Durand Jones & The Indications also made its debut at the popular Mexican festival, drawing thousands to the NIVEA stage with a blend of contemporary R&B and soul. The group brought a sexy, danceable vibe to the evening with its upbeat, retro-soul sound, getting the crowd moving to songs like “Circles,” “The Way That I Do,” “Love Will Work It Out” and “Flower Moon.”.

Uber is testing rides for kids as young as 10

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that getting kids where they need to go is a job in itself.
  • Uber is testing whether it can take on some of that driving.
  • Industry observers note that the company's latest pilot, Uber Kids, lets parents and guardians book rides for children ages 10 to 12 to take on their own.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that getting kids where they need to go is a job in itself. Between school, extracurriculars, and appointments, families often piece together rides with help from relatives and other parents.

Uber is testing whether it can take on some of that driving.

Industry observers note that the company's latest pilot, Uber Kids, lets parents and guardians book rides for children ages 10 to 12 to take on their own. The service is available to select families in Austin, Texas, Nashville, Tennessee, and Madison, Wisconsin, starting Nov. 19. This comes after some rumors: Bloomberg first reported in August that Uber was developing the option.

Here's what parents should know before booking, from how to set up a ride to how to follow it in real time.

In a recent development, to book a ride, a parent or guardian first adds their child to the Family hub in the Uber app. Then they select the child as the rider. If the pilot is available to their family, Uber Kids will appear as a ride option, and the app will guide them through adding pickup and drop-off details.

Recent findings suggest that kids don't need their own Uber account or app. They can get updates about the trip by text at the number listed on their profile. Parents can request rides from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily, as long as a driver is available.

Each ride goes straight to one destination. A parent or the adult handling pickup can ride along, and kids ages 10 to 17 can join with their guardian’s permission, as long as the child the ride was booked for is in the car. And, if no Uber Kids driver is available, a child ages 10 to 12 needs an adult to ride with them in a regular Uber.

A parent or another adult selected in the app must be at pickup to give the driver the PIN that starts the ride. If someone else needs to handle pickup or drop-off after booking, the guardian contacts the driver and sends the fresh adult the trip details and tracking link. Only the guardian can change the destination in the app.

Recent findings suggest that once the car is moving, the guardian can track it on a map, contact the driver, or tap "Watch" to see live video from the driver's phone. The driver gets a notification when the feed starts, and only the guardian and safety agents can watch it. Uber can flag an unexpected stop or route change so a safety agent can check in. Kids can also call their guardian or the support number in their trip texts. According to recent reports, at drop-off, the driver confirms the child reached the entrance or met the adult assigned to greet them. If that person hasn't arrived, the driver tries to reach them or the guardian, then calls Uber's safety line if nobody answers.

The app also makes a separate audio and video recording. Neither the guardian nor the driver can access it. Uber notes it receives the encrypted recording only if someone reports a safety incident. Otherwise, it’s deleted after 14 days.

Recent findings suggest that uber indicates it invites experienced, highly rated drivers who have passed a background check. Drivers have to complete a training module on how Uber Kids trips work and turn on audio and video recording in the Driver app. Uber's driver guide explains how drivers should handle pickup and drop-off.

It's interesting that Uber is expanding to younger riders as it faces thousands of lawsuits from passengers who say they were sexually assaulted by drivers.

In a recent development, as of Nov. 2, 4,548 cases were pending in the coordinated federal litigation, according to the U.S. Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation. In February, a federal jury in Arizona found Uber liable and awarded $8.5 million to a woman who noted a driver raped her when she was 19. And in April, a North Carolina jury awarded $5,000 in a related case after finding that a driver committed battery. (Uber settled another federal case in October before it went to trial.).

Uber has been giving teens a way to get around on their own since 2023. Kids ages 13 to 17 can request rides through an account linked to a parent's account, and Lyft offers a similar service in select areas called "Lyft Teen." When a child in the Uber Kids pilot turns 13, they can set up a teen account and request their own ride (or their parents can still do it for them).

According to recent reports, families with younger kids already have options like HopSkipDrive, which takes riders as young as 6. The manufacturer says its drivers need at least five years of caregiving experience and must pass a fingerprint-based background check. There's no saying whether Uber utilizes similar investigations.

For plenty of families, getting to practice or a lesson still means a parent does the driving. In a 2025 survey by AP-NORC and HopSkipDrive, 75 percent of parents whose kids participated in extracurriculars stated they drove their kids themselves. When asked about the school commute, 28 percent of K–12 parents said they considered a hired ride, like a taxi, Uber, or Lyft, at least somewhat safe for their child.

This pilot will ultimately test whether features like a PIN at pickup and live video during the ride make parents comfortable enough to book one.

Autistic brains look surprisingly similar on average. Then scientists looked closer.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (770 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that brain scans have revealed a surprising pattern in people with autism.
  • In a recent development, the findings, published in JNeurosci, suggest that looking at average brain activity may conceal notable differences among people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
  • The research was led by Dorit Kliemann and James Traer of the University of Iowa, who worked with collaborators to investigate how brain activity differs between adults with and without autism.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that brain scans have revealed a surprising pattern in people with autism. Although adults with and without autism showed remarkably similar brain activity when researchers compared group averages, a closer examination uncovered striking differences between individuals. These differences were especially pronounced in brain regions involved in understanding and responding to social information.

In a recent development, the findings, published in JNeurosci, suggest that looking at average brain activity may conceal notable differences among people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The discovery could help scientists better understand why autism varies so widely from person to person and eventually support more personalized approaches to care.

The research was led by Dorit Kliemann and James Traer of the University of Iowa, who worked with collaborators to investigate how brain activity differs between adults with and without autism.

What Brain Scans Reveal When People Watch Movies.

To explore these differences, the team examined previously collected brain imaging data from Indiana University and Caltech. The recordings captured brain activity as adults with and without autism watched movies from several genres, including animation, action, romantic comedy, and Hitchcockian thrillers.

Recent findings suggest that movies offered researchers a way to study how the brain responds to a constantly changing stream of sights, sounds, and social interactions. Unlike simple laboratory tasks, movies present a rich mixture of information that more closely resembles the complexity of everyday experiences.

Using the imaging data, the researchers trained a computational model to identify connections between brain activity and different elements of the movies. These included visual details, sounds, and more abstract social information, such as interactions between characters.

After training, the model was able to accurately predict activity across several brain systems.

Kliemann explained why this approach is particularly useful for investigating the social challenges sometimes associated with autism: "The computational model allowed us to look for robust brain responses to many different aspects of the complex, dynamic contexts in the movies.".

A Surprising Difference Hidden by Brain Activity Averages.

The most unexpected finding emerged when researchers compared the two groups.

Industry observers note that at first, the results suggested relatively little difference. When brain responses were averaged across participants, the model predicted activity in various brain systems similarly for adults with and without autism.

However, the picture changed when the researchers examined how much individual participants differed from others in their own group.

Industry observers note that people with autism demonstrated substantially greater variation in their brain responses than participants without autism. In other words, although the overall group averages looked similar, the responses of individual autistic participants were much less alike.

This increased variability appeared across nearly every brain system examined. The strongest differences occurred in the social brain system, a network of regions involved in processing social information and understanding other people.

Why the Findings Could Change Autism Research.

The results raise notable questions about how scientists investigate autism. Many existing approaches to understanding and treating the condition rely heavily on comparing average measurements from groups of autistic and nonautistic individuals.

But if autistic people show considerable differences in how their brains process information, these averages may obscure some of the most meaningful findings.

Traer described the team's surprise: "We were surprised by the similarity of group averages. The results suggest that we need to focus on understanding the details of individual brain responses. How and why do they differ?".

Rather than searching only for brain activity patterns shared by everyone with autism, the findings point toward the potential value of studying individuals and identifying smaller groups with similar characteristics.

Kliemann highlighted what this could mean for future research and support: "Identifying ASD subgroups may help us build a more precise understanding of the condition and help develop ways to provide individually tailored support.".

Recent findings suggest that the researchers now proposal to investigate how these differences in brain activity relate to variations in autism-related behavior. They hope to determine where and when the differences emerge, how they are connected to individual characteristics, and what might explain them.

Ultimately, the findings suggest that understanding autism may require looking beyond the average brain and paying closer attention to the distinctive ways individuals process the world.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ever since P.J. Byrne had a literal meltdown in the most showstopping scene of Damien Chazelle’s Babylon, his career as a scene-stealing character actor has reached a upcoming high.

Recent findings suggest that the Upcoming Jersey native’s 2026 alone has brought eight credits, including the conclusion of his recurring character on The Boys, Coyote vs. Acme, The End of Oak Street and a series-regular role on USA’s basic cable hit The Rainmaker. Most notably, he now stars in his biggest film role to date as Oscar-winning Rocky producer Irwin Winkler in Peter Farrelly’s biographical awards contender, I Play Rocky. Related Stories Movies 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Feasting With $120M+ in Franchise's Box Office Comeback Hollywood Flashback Yo, Academy! When 'Rocky' Was Crowned Best Picture Champ.

Recent findings suggest that in 1975, Winkler and his producing partner Robert Chartoff were developing Martin Scorsese’s New York, New York at the same time as the underdog story from a then-unknown Sylvester Stallone. The former would become the first of a half-dozen films Winkler collaborated on with Scorsese, including 2013’s The Wolf of Wall Street. It’s fitting, then, that Byrne is now playing the celebrated producer, given that his own career turning point came with his role as Rugrat in Scorsese and Leonardo DiCaprio’s unhinged take on the life of former stockbroker Jordan Belfort. (Byrne would later reunite with Scorsese on his 2016 series Vinyl.).

Byrne’s turn as a founding member of Belfort’s Stratton Oakmont is probably best remembered for one particularly rambunctious trading-floor scene in which his character shaves a female sales assistant’s head. The opportunity also allowed Byrne to put his unused finance degree from Boston College to work, albeit in a fictionalized version of a career path he had promptly abandoned because of his aversion to boiler-room culture.

Industry observers note that in the mid-’90s, one of his Boston College professors encouraged him to try his hand at drama school instead, leading him to DePaul University in Chicago. Byrne’s time in the Windy City seems to have left a lasting impression. He often speaks about acting in the same terms that Chicago Bulls legend Michael Jordan once used to describe his record-setting 3-point barrage against the Portland Trail Blazers in Game 1 of the 1992 NBA Finals. When Byrne acts, he strives to enter a flow state, or “the zone,” as Jordan called it, where he’s so locked in to the task at hand that distractions fade and he can achieve peak performance.

Byrne’s Wolf of Wall Street video audition featured a monologue he reimagined from the ground up. Channeling his brief experience in the financial world, he portrayed his stockbroker character emotionally manipulating a widow into forking over $100,000 during a sales call. Scorsese appreciated the creative risk so much that he recited part of the speech back to Byrne during their eventual in-person callback. Byrne’s improvisational instincts and willingness to take creative leaps through punch-ups and alternative dialogue are muscles he first developed during his early days in Los Angeles.

In a recent development, at the turn of the century, Byrne put himself through the wringer of commercial auditions. With a talent pool far deeper than most people might expect, he knew he needed to find a way to stand out. That meant arriving with his own variations on the material or improvising in the moment. To pay the bills between sporadic acting jobs, he provided script coverage and handled other development duties at the production organization of family friend and fellow Boston College alum Chris O’Donnell.

Eventually, he left his VP position to focus solely on acting. Nameless parts soon gave way to small but named roles, though there were milestones along the way that reinforced his greater pursuit. One came when he made Will Ferrell and Stephen Colbert laugh during a table-read scene in Nora Ephron’s Bewitched (2005). Byrne played a TV writer in the film, an early example of the showbiz-affiliated roles that would become a calling card throughout his career. He speculates that his time working in development may have influenced that pattern.

Sources indicate that byrne’s road to I Play Rocky can also be traced back to commercials cast by casting director Rick Montgomery. It further involved producer Toby Emmerich’s tenure as head of Newly introduced Line, during which Byrne made memorable appearances in the label’s Horrible Bosses and Final Destination 5. Above all, Byrne won a major fan in Farrelly when he played a record executive in the best picture-winning Green Book, followed by Dear Santa, the Christmas comedy Farrelly co-wrote for his brother Bobby to direct.

Recent findings suggest that “After Green Book, Peter was like, ‘You need your Paul Giamatti [in Sideways] part. You need a bigger part in a movie,’” Byrne tells The Hollywood Reporter.

According to recent reports, the role of Irwin Winkler still didn’t come easy. In the behind-the-scenes narrative, Winkler and Chartoff desperately want to produce Stallone’s Rocky screenplay, but he refuses to sell it unless he gets to star as the title character. Winkler and Chartoff, ever the pragmatists, try to give the aspiring young actor and screenwriter a reality check about how star power drives the financing and green-lighting of most movies. But Stallone stands his ground despite increasingly lucrative offers for the script.

Sources indicate that eventually, Winkler and Chartoff realize they shouldn’t be producing an underdog story about a small-time boxer named Rocky Balboa if they aren’t willing to practice what they preach. So they risk everything, including their names and their homes, to install Stallone as the star, all while distributor United Artists sets him up to fail at every turn in hopes of replacing him with a proven commodity.

Industry observers note that the casting of Byrne’s role also became rather meta because the I Play Rocky brain trust initially sought a name for Winkler. With relative unknown Anthony Ippolito already cast as young Sly, it’s understandable why they would want to shore up the surrounding roles with established, butts-in-seats actors. But the producers of I Play Rocky ultimately arrived at the same conclusion as the producers of Rocky — gamble on talent, not status.

Sources indicate that “They wanted to get a name, because there weren’t a lot of names [in this cast]. But they were also living in the world of, If we’re going to cast Anthony Ippolito as Sylvester Stallone, then let’s give other people shots too,” Byrne says. “They all knew me from these small parts. Then they just believed in me enough to give me a shot. I want to tell the world that there’s honestly no small parts. Someone will ultimately give you a chance.”.

Industry observers note that below, in a conversation with THR, Byrne also discusses the day his improvisational skills resulted in I Play Rocky’s most hilarious scene. He also addresses whether the strained relationship between Winkler and Stallone in recent years influenced his take at all.

It’s not talent. I just have three children. I have to pay for their lives. That’s all that is. It’s like, Yes, I’ll do that. I have three children.

You’ve still cemented yourself as one of the industry’s go-to character actors.

Can you feel that wind in your sail?

I always say ABC: always be classy. So I don’t know if I can admit to that, but I do have repeat buyers, if you will, because they’re buddies. Once I work on anything, I tend to have repeat business. So I’ll meet you halfway. I hate giving myself flowers like that, but I believe in myself to deliver. And if other people see that, then I appreciate it.

It has been revealed that when you hear labels like “character actor” or “comic relief” or “scene-stealer,” do you bristle at all? Or do you embrace the lane you’ve carved out for yourself?

Recent findings suggest that it’s funny. I don’t even look at it that way. All ships rise with the tide. I want everyone to score and win. I’m always surrounded by incredible actors in everything I do, so everyone passes the ball nicely. It’s not about being funny or stealing scenes. It’s, How do I make these moments pop more? This sounds so cheesy and trite, but it’s really, How do I service the director or the writer? I’ve been doing this so long that they are often my really good friends.

In a recent development, when someone makes a movie, they’ve put four years of their life into it. They’ve battled producers and studio executives to get this one day of this particular scene, and half their budget is being spent on a goddamn crane shot. So I just want to do everything I can for them. I put in the work, and my brain just naturally looks for moments that can pop. Is there an ability to make this zeitgeisty so that people can relate to it and it can become its own thing?

Where did this mentality come from?

I started out in Los Angeles doing commercials, and I was baptized by fire doing them. Commercials are like street basketball. It’s rough. They’re not nice to you. The rooms aren’t sweet. They’re not kind. But some of the best actors are commercial actors. They just never found the right lane or the right agent. They’re still out there, and they’re extraordinary actors. But adding jokes during commercial auditions is how I trained my brain to find moments to pop. I would think of the fifth funniest joke in my brain because the first four would probably be thought of by someone else.

That mindset succeeds in scenarios where I have fearless directors who’ve proven themselves. It’s usually the great directors like Marty Scorsese or Peter Farrelly or Damien Chazelle who don’t have to worry about notes from everyone. They know I’ve done the work and have their vision in mind, so they’ll take the handcuffs off me. They’ll be like, “Just add stuff. We trust you. Go.” They know that before a job, I’ll literally sit in a hotel room for two weeks and have food sent up while I make sure I’m doing everything I can for them. I don’t want to let anyone down.

Sources indicate that you’re also asked to play showbiz people fairly often. The Boys, Babylon, The Significant Cigar and A Complete Unknown are only a few examples, as is your current role as Irwin Winkler in I Play Rocky. Do you have any theories why this has become your niche?

I feel like I have a face like that. I also do a lot of period pieces and play a lot of lawyers. That’s just what’s filming now. But I think it’s all because I know those characters well from when I started out in Los Angeles.

I owe a lot to Chris O’Donnell. When he was Robin [in Batman & Robin], he had a production firm at Warner Bros. His sisters and my sister are really good friends. And because I had a finance degree from Boston College, I was like, If acting doesn’t work out, I can be an intern with them. To his credit, his company gave me a script and were like, “Hey, do coverage on this script.” So I did, and the coverage was called “brilliant.” But it was only brilliant because I literally just went to grad school where I learned arc and character. I literally just wrote papers for three years.

Sources indicate that chris was like, “Be our story editor.” And I was like, “Chris, I came here to act.” Then he gave me the greatest gift ever when he stated, “No, come and go as you please.” So I was able to walk onto the Warner Bros. and work for him, while also doing commercials and small TV jobs. Every time I tried to quit, they were like, “You’re a vice president right now.”.

Recent findings suggest that I set up movies. I learned the business. I would walk past The West Wing and ER stages, and I told myself that I wouldn’t set foot on those stages until I was invited. And I did eventually book those jobs. So I became comfortable being in that environment, and it wasn’t so daunting going into those rooms.

It’s because of all those early experiences that I have a lot of friends who are producers, writers and directors. So I know this world well, and when someone states, “Play this showbiz part,” I’m like, “Trust me, I got it.”.

You worked with Peter Farrelly on Green Book and Dear Santa. Did he go straight to you for Irwin Winkler?

It has been revealed that it wasn’t straight to me, but I love Peter forever. I want to tell the world that there’s honestly no small parts, and you never know what’s going to come around. And that’s why this movie was so super meta for me. They wanted to get a name, because there weren’t a lot of names [in this cast]. But they were also living in the world of, If we’re going to cast Anthony Ippolito as Sylvester Stallone, then let’s give other people shots too.

In a recent development, after Green Book, Peter was like, “You need your Paul Giamatti [in Sideways] part. You need a bigger part in a movie.” [I Play Rocky casting director] Rick Montgomery cast me in commercials years ago, and [producer] Toby Emmerich also ran Upcoming Line when I had small parts in Horrible Bosses and Final Destination 5.

So they all knew me from these small parts, and they all said, “He’s ready to have a bigger part. Come audition for this.” Then they just believed in me enough to give me a shot. Someone will ultimately give you a chance, just like they once gave it to Sylvester Stallone and now Anthony Ippolito and me.

Everything is driven by the same dozen names now, so it’s nice to hear that Farrelly is looking elsewhere.

Industry observers note that yeah, he’s incredibly loyal. If you look at his movies, the same people always come back. When you go out for drinks with Pete, 32 people show up with him. I love that idea of a family. Working with friends is the best way to go to work, and that’s another reason why I get repeat business.

It has been revealed that when it’s four in the morning on a Friday night and you’ve been shooting 12 hours, we’re still cheerleaders for each other. I love those kinds of sets. It kills me when I see people being cancers or want to get off set. Again, I know what my friend went through to be here after four years. So I always say, “Let’s deliver this moment the best way we can because we’re never coming back.”.

What went through your mind when you first witnessed Anthony Ippolito’s take on Sly?

It was at a table read, and while everybody does a version of Sylvester Stallone, I was like, We’re living and dying on this kid. This is the moment. And as soon as he opened his mouth, it was so subtle and soulful and full of heart. It honestly surpassed what my expectation was going to be. I have been doing this a long time, and this is the biggest part I’ve ever gotten in a movie. It’s so beautiful for me, personally. But I can’t help but get so psyched for this kid because he’s so spectacular.

I’ve been around some incredible performances. I watched Leo just destroy on The Wolf of Wall Street. And Margot Robbie, I still wish she got her flowers for Babylon. There’s even a scene with me and Laura Dern on Massive Little Lies. When you’re an actor in a scene with them and the camera’s not on you, there’s just a moment when you become an audience member. And you’re like, Oh shit, it’s happening. You can feel it in the room and you want to deliver for them and be there for them. And that’s what happened with Anthony.

He was in the zone. That’s what basketball players say when the net looks like the size of an ocean and they can’t miss. That’s what it felt like watching Anthony. He was so good that I kept thinking, Did Sylvester Stallone travel through space and time to possess this kid’s body? That’s how special it was. Then Pete would call cut, and Anthony would come back online and say, “Hey, what are we getting for dinner tonight?” And I was just like, “What is going on right now?” Peter and I were like, “Is he the world’s greatest actor?” He also played Rocky and Sylvester Stallone, and it was just crazy to watch him play two different characters.

Recent findings suggest that I also watched Timothée Chalamet be Bob Dylan, and that was another time where I was like, “Holy shit.” But Timmy would stay in character, unlike Anthony. So everyone has their own method, and there is no right way.

There’s no love lost between Stallone and Winkler in recent years. Sly resents the fact that Winkler retains full ownership of the Rocky franchise and that he doesn’t have a piece of the pie to leave for his family. Did you and Farrelly ever discuss planting that seed of acrimony for where their relationship would end up?

In a recent development, producers are observers. They are there to eliminate risk, put out fires and make sure that the art happens. Sometimes, they have to guide it and have their influence, but that’s what they are. Bob Chartoff and Irwin Winkler were the greatest producers and the ultimate backstop to any ball getting past the catcher. So that’s what I had to deal with in my role.

Sources indicate that the first time you meet my character, he’s all business. He’s not mean to Sly, but he just doesn’t look the part for the role being cast. But then he’s intrigued by this smart guy sitting in front of him, and then they eventually read his scripts to see that there’s talent there. At first, Winkler believes in the project, and then he learns to believe in the person behind it.

The end of the movie shows the real-life clip of when Rocky won best picture at the 1977 Oscars. Bob Chartoff and Irwin Winkler stood up, and Irwin Winkler immediately grabbed Sylvester Stallone to join them on stage, which is rare. It’s usually just the producers who accept the best picture award.

In a recent development, but Winkler grabbed Sylvester Stallone and put his arm around him with such love. It was like, This is my son. I believe in you so much. I mortgaged my house for you. I didn’t just bet on a movie. I bet on a child that I love. It’s the idea that you would do anything for your kids, and like I said, I literally work for my children. The money comes in the door, and it goes right to give them every opportunity to succeed in life.

Industry observers note that whatever the extraneous stuff is between them now, I was meant to portray that period of time in the late ‘70s. I was there to share the message that if you really fucking do the work and you believe in yourself — and then you surround yourself with like-minded people who truly believe in you as well — then anything is possible. Maybe you too will one day win an Oscar. That was a special moment in all of their lives, and that’s what I needed to play and had to play.

Recent findings suggest that in a perfect world, a clause would kick in after x amount of years so that the original creator receives at least a sliver of the pie. But like you noted, Winkler and Chartoff risked their homes on a complete unknown. They also gave him profit participation on the first film, as well as most, if not all, of the future films. So I hate to both-sides the issue, but I really do see both sides here.

Recent findings suggest that of course, I thought about all of that and who these people are today and yesterday. But my job was to play that moment in time in which greatness happened. It was a beautiful thing, even if you’re always battling for what you want and going at it. That’s why I have that moment after Winkler found out that Sly and Carl Weathers had never boxed before.

In a recent development, yeah, Winkler went out and got the world’s greatest boxing choreographer, but then Sly kicked him out. All the script had was Winkler saying, “It’s a boxing movie!” So I remarked to Peter, “The producer’s job is to put out fires, so he would lose his mind right now. This is a handcuffs-off moment. Let me riff and play a little bit here.” It was a scary moment because it was late at night right before Thanksgiving, and everybody wanted to go home for Thanksgiving. But here I was adding a lot to the scene.

Recent findings suggest that to Peter’s credit, he let me go. I made that line up about The Godfather: “It’s not about the mafia. It’s about a nice Italian family that loves pasta.” Then, because he’s angry, he has to get the fuck out of the room. So I went up the stairs toward the door, and I added the lines about how this “happens to be” a set of stairs and how this “happens to be” a door as he walks out. So you do go at it when you’re making films because you’re passionate about the product.

It has been revealed that yeah, the “happens to be” scene is your “hello, college!” scene of this movie. Winkler’s meltdown is rooted in director John G. Avildsen’s position that Rocky isn’t a boxing movie. He made the point that it’s a character study about a guy who “happens to be” a boxer. Plus, it hits close to home because every entertainment journalist has written some version of that “happens to be” line about a story in which the surrounding world is incidental.

Sources indicate that those improvised lines came from being in the zone. It’s the best when it happens. I also didn’t know that guy was going to ask me to take off his jacket. We were just playing in the moment. They let this little chemistry experiment happen.

Recent findings suggest that the Rocky and Apollo fight is ultimately saved for the closing credits, serving as the punchline to the “happens to be” bit. I Play Rocky is also a character study that happens to have boxing in it.

Industry observers note that was that fight always intended for the credits? Or did they realize in the edit that it would make for a great gag?

Industry observers note that it had another great ending as well. Rocky was boxing, and when they called cut, he didn’t want to hear it. Then he was like, “I can go again.” He’d been going and going for 28 days, and then his wife came up to say, “It’s over.” And he was like, “No, no, I can do one more.”And she was like, “No, it’s over. You did it.” I could cry right now just thinking about how they ended it.

But Anthony’s earlier moment where he was hitting the door as Rocky and going, “It stinks! My life stinks!” — how were we going to top how extraordinary that was? We couldn’t top that. Showing it toward the end also has a beautiful message, so that’s moviemaking. You’re learning and adapting and changing as you’re going.

It has been revealed that peter also edits as he’s going, and he knows the movie so well. Like Avildsen in the movie, I would add something, and Peter would be like, “We got it. Cut. Moving on.” And I’d be like, “What do you mean you got it? I only said the line once.” And he was like, “No, no, it’s great.” This is the first movie I saw six weeks after filming it, so I remembered every second of filming. And when some of those moments came up, I was like, He was right. That is great. We didn’t need another angle.

If you had to guess, how much of Rocky did Farrelly recreate?

It has been revealed that oh God, if I was going to throw out a number, maybe 26.9 percent. I don’t know. They shot that boxing scene for a week, and that was the longest, most expensive part of the shoot.

I wish I could’ve seen Amazon’s response to it ending up in the closing credits.

Recent findings suggest that (Laughs.) Again, to Peter’s credit, he mentioned, “What do we think the best part of the story is?” That’s an amazing thing. The great directors are fearless. They don’t operate from fear. They trust their instincts and their gut. They have great editors too.

Some locations probably don’t exist in the same form anymore, but for places like Rocky’s apartment, did you revisit as many original spots as possible from Rocky?

Sources indicate that we shot at the same apartment he lived in, and it’s still a rough neighborhood to this day. We heard people around the neighborhood say, “Oh my God, this feels just like yesterday.” Some of the same people lived there 50 years ago.

Recent findings suggest that then we went to the Rocky Steps [at the Philadelphia Museum of Art], which was amazing. AnnaSophia Robb and I ran up the stairs with Anthony. Then I came back down the stairs, and Tracy Letts was there, so I have the greatest video of me and Tracy Letts running up the stairs together. I have to post it. It’s so beautiful that all these people come from around the world to run up the stairs in their gray sweatsuits. I have another little video of Anthony waiting in line to take a picture next to the statue of Rocky, dressed as Rocky.

So it was really special to be in Philadelphia. It’s a super-duper city, man. You feel the lunch-pale vibe. We all knew how special this movie is to so many people around the world, and while Sylvester, Irwin Winkler and SteadiCam creator Garrett Brown are still alive, we didn’t want to let them down. We truly felt that way.

Overall, the movie is largely about the power of no. Sly stated no to Winkler and Chartoff countless times before he got the deal he thought he wanted at the time. Have you had a chance to say no to something that ultimately proved to be the best decision?

My whole life is built on not understanding what the word no means. I was supposed to work on Wall Street, but then I decided to walk away to be an actor. I was told, “You can’t be an actor,” and I was like, “Yes, I can.”.

Industry observers note that to me, no just means not now, and my whole life is built on that premise. Nothing is impossible. That’s why I love the movie business, and that’s what made Irwin and Bob incredible producers. They didn’t understand the word no either. If something went wrong on a film, they fixed it.

According to recent reports, marty Scorsese talks about this all the time [from his experiences with Winkler]. He notes, “All this craziness was happening in the background, and Irwin Winkler never let me know any of it. I was just there to be free and think about the project.” So I wanted to put a little of that into I Play Rocky [when Winkler and Chartoff opt not to tell Sly they’ve mortgaged their homes to keep the movie going].

According to recent reports, I’ve always loved movies and shows about the making of famous movies or shows. Of all your other projects, is there one that would make for a compelling behind-the-scenes narrative à la I Play Rocky?

It has been revealed that oh, it’d be Coyote vs. Acme. My dear friend, Dave Green, directed it, and the world almost never saw it. It was going to be thrown in a vault because an accountant made a decision. We should always be art over commerce, especially when you’ve chosen to make movies for a living. I had a front row seat to what Dave went through, and he was so classy through the whole process.

Sources indicate that another heartbreaking aspect to the story is that [Looney Tunes character voice actor] Eric Bauza just passed away. It’s a bummer. He was a generational talent, and he was also one of the classiest, nicest guys you’ve ever met. It just kills me. He has an eight-year-old kid and a fiancée. He literally stood up for the movie while presenting at an award show and said, “Release Coyote vs. Acme!” He said that to the corporation that paid him all his money and fed him because he voiced Looney Tunes characters.

On set, it was amazing what we did because we had no money. I wasn’t even playing that part [of Acme lawyer, Bill Pelicanos] the week before. They were like, “John Cena is going to do it. Do you want to be a sidekick?” And I was like, “Yes! I want my hair to look exactly like his, and I also want to be bald in a scene.” And they were like, “We can’t afford any of that.” And I was like, “I’m calling in favors for hair.” Everyone was doing favors for everybody on that movie. We believed in the art.

Sources indicate that it was so meta because it was about fighting massive corporations. Everyone was doing that movie for the right reason. So that would truly make for a special behind-the-scenes movie. I also just found out it can get nominated for best animated feature because over 75 percent of the project is animated. I really hope it gets its flowers.

If Babylon got the I Play Rocky treatment, what would the behind the scenes of the “hello, college!” sequence look like?

Industry observers note that well, we shot that 10-minute scene over three days. It was one of the greatest, most fun shooting experiences of my life because, once again, Damien let me go. I auditioned during COVID, when you couldn’t be in the room together, and I got a note back from Damien saying, “It feels like you want to really let it go.” At first, I was like, I want to stay close to the lines because this is Damien Chazelle. I’ve never auditioned for him. I love this dude. I want to be in his movie so badly.

It has been revealed that but once he noted, “Go,” I added so many horrible things. Then I handed it in, and 20 minutes later, I got the call that I got the part. When I showed up on set, I saw that the lines I had added were in the movie, and that’s when I knew I was going to riff even more. Damien ended up letting everybody play.

My close-ups were on the last day, and I had basically already lost my voice. It ended up being gone for a month. But something came out of me that day to make it all happen. When I did the first take of my close-up, they were like, “Great. That was amazing. We got it.” But I was like, “Let’s keep going. I have four more ideas. I’m going to lose my voice. I want to get it all.” We still had a game left to play, and I didn’t want to celebrate yet.

According to recent reports, everybody knew how special and spectacular that scene was, and everyone was cheering for everybody when it was their take. Those special days also had moments in the zone. I was able to be conscious of how amazing this was and still deliver new stuff.

Did they actually keep the stage extra warm given the nature of the scene?

I mean, it was hot, but that was mostly just incredible makeup. They put this gel on your head that looks like sweat. Those were three days of magic, man. Damien had a massive board of all the shots he wanted, and we just checked them off as we went. It was awesome.

It has been revealed that what about The Wolf of Wall Street? How would you dramatize one of those days?

That was an amazing brotherhood. I’m still friends with so many of those guys. Jon Bernthal lived across the hall from me. Kenny Choi lived downstairs. Brian Sacca and Ethan Suplee were also close, and we had a blast. We knew how powerful that story was.

Sources indicate that leo sometimes likes to stay in character, but he joked, “If I stayed in character this whole time, I would have a nervous breakdown.” So we got the real Leo. We got to bro out with a buddy. He’s the man of our times. He’s the great actor. He’s charming. He’s the best storyteller. He wanted us all to have a great time. He was also producing, so he made sure that we met the real Jordan Belfort and learned how to sell from the guy. The idea was that we needed to really see who this guy is and how these people truly operate.

Industry observers note that as I mentioned earlier, the greatness of Marty is that he let us all riff and play. So I riffed with Jonah [Hill] and Leo, and that was another magical experience because I probably made up 80 percent of the lines I stated in that movie. Marty was always like, “It’s too clean. Mess it up. Go.”.

In a recent development, when I auditioned, I used my finance degree to make up my own monologue, and Marty knew it. So he memorized it and read it back to me. I was like, This is the greatest day of my life. Then, on the first day of rehearsal, Marty and Leo asked me questions about finance. I was like, I can’t believe I’m sitting here answering their finance questions. This is crazy. Am I an actor? Am I a consultant? What is happening?

Years from now, when you write your memoir, how will you sum up the 2026 chapter?

“He was the hardest working person on the set, and he was always classy.” The title of the biography should be P.J. Byrne: Over the Shoulder and Out of Focus.

***I Play Rocky is now playing in movie theaters nationwide.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Pattinson will be the seventh actor to play the role.
  • Recent findings suggest that "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime," Pattinson mentioned in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robert Pattinson has been cast as the next James Bond in the upcoming film from director Denis Villeneuve. It will be the 26th James Bond film and the first since Amazon MGM took over the iconic franchise.

Pattinson will be the seventh actor to play the role. Monday's announcement — which came in part via an Instagram post — ends a long period of speculation about who would take over as "007" after Daniel Craig.

Recent findings suggest that "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime," Pattinson mentioned in a statement. "I couldn't be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.".

Pattinson has appeared in several significant-ticket films this year, including Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" and psychological thriller "Primetime," and he'll soon appear in "Dune: Part Three," also directed by Villeneuve. Pattinson, who rose to fame with the Twilight movie series, is also in production for Matt Reeves' "The Batman Part II," a follow-up to the 2022 film based on the DC comic.

The upcoming Bond film will have a script by Steven Knight and will be produced by Amy Pascal, known for her work on the Spider-Man franchise, and David Heyman, who produced all eight Harry Potter films.

Recent findings suggest that "We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007," Villeneuve noted. "I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.".

In a recent development, in 2022, Amazon bought MGM Studios, which had long produced the Bond movies, for roughly $8.45 billion. Amazon MGM then acquired creative control of the James Bond intellectual property rights in 2025, when it closed a deal with longtime producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson.

The film is still untitled, and Amazon MGM hasn't unveiled a projected release date.

#70626. The $500 billion beauty industry's 'green' ambitions are a patchwork at best. And they're falling short
